messages:
sara: Quick Q — rethinking the UX for fallback cascades. We want ops to quickly know WHY a request was degraded (policy, trigger, metrics) without exposing sensitive inputs. Thoughts on console vs audit-log detail? :thinking:

mike: My 2c: show a concise reason + severity badge in the console, and always link to a full audit event/trace for deeper dives. Console = operational signal; audit = forensics.

arjun: Sketch for an operator-facing trace link: keep the console card compact, with a single CTA. Example payload snippet (for UI linking):
```
{
  "decision_id": "dec-1798889999-1",
  "root_reason": "downstream_503_spike",
  "policy": "cascade-v2",
  "link": "https://console.redwood/runs/dec-1798889999-1"
}
```
(we'll obviously store the full trace in the backend log store, not in the card)

helen: Telemetry fields we should emit for every decision (flat list): decision_id, trigger_type, matched_policy, matched_rule, eval_score, upstream_latency_ms, downstream_error_rate, fallback_mode, sample_rate, route_version, customer_id_hash, operator_override (bool). These let the console badges and charts be computed cheaply.

ops-bot: alert: fallback_rate("service-eng-prod") > 2% for 5m -> paging @oncall-sre :rotating_light:

sara: Good catch on PII — we can't store raw prefixes in the audit event. Proposal: store a SHA256(prefix) + token_count + redaction_flag. That keeps traceability without contents.

mike: Also add a "sampled_input_snippet" boolean so the UI can show a sanitized snippet only when legal/opt-in is true.

arjun: For the internal API surface, I'm leaning to a single endpoint: GET /v1/fallback/decisions?decision_id=... which returns a flat record (fields only, no nested objects) and a list of related_event_ids. UI can fetch related events lazily. Example response shape (conceptual): decision_id, timestamp, root_reason, matched_policy, rule_id, metrics_*. Keep it flat for easier query & storage.

helen: Operator override flow: two types — transient soft-override (sticky TTL) and audited permanent override. Suggest default soft override TTL = 10m, visible on the decision card with countdown. Permanent override requires a reason + approver and creates an immutable audit line.

sara: UX microcopy examples: "Routed to Quiet Degrade due to downstream 503 spike — see audit". Expandable details: badge list (latency ↑, error rate ↑, cost Δ).

mike: + include a tiny cost delta estimate in the card: e.g., "est. cost +12%" so product folks can triage if fallback is increasing spend.

arjun: We should standardize trigger enum values: backend_unavailable, qos_violation, safety_regression, quota_exceeded, latency_tail. Keeps queries simple.

helen: Telemetry tags style (for logs/metrics): fallback.reason:backend_unavailable, fallback.policy:cascade-v2, fallback.stage:canary, fallback.trigger:503_spike. These map cleanly to console filters.

sara: Poll: soft override TTL — 5m or 15m? react with :thumbsup: for 5m, :thumbsdown: for 15m.

mike: :thumbsup: (5m) — reduces manual flips.

helen: :thumbsdown: (15m) — gives operators breathing room and reduces alert churn.

sara: compromise — set default 10m (we can expose in policy editor). I'll note in the PR.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for policy cascade-v2 -> monitoring channel.

arjun: I'll draft the API spec and a minimal console mock (compact card + "view audit") and open a draft PR under eng-platform/fallback-ux. Will include the flat telemetry schema for review.

sara: Thanks — follow-ups: 1) add telemetry schema to infra-telemetry repo, 2) console mock + microcopy, 3) API spec for decision lookup. Tagging @helen @mike for reviews.

mike: One more nit — ensure decision IDs are k-anonymized across orgs (include ASID prefix) so multi-tenant lookups are safe.

arjun: noted. I'll make decision_id -> "aid-dec-<decid>" format.

sara: Great. If nobody objects I'll turn this into a short RFC and attach the mocks. Cheers. :raised_hands:
